items.text: The CTest CNAEXT_NoPosixSetenv (scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py, registered in modules/graphics-ext/examples/CMakeLists.txt whenever CNA_BUILD_TESTS is on and a Python 3 interpreter was found, label CnaExt) fails at 009d40f5. The gate forbids any setenv(/unsetenv( call under modules/, tools/ and tests/, but the snapshot has twelve: WaylandPlatform.cpp unsets XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN, and WaylandDesktopPortalTests.cpp, WaylandProtocolTests.cpp, WaylandTestCompositor.cpp and WaylandTestEnvironment.cpp set or unset WAYLAND_SOCKET, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, LC_ALL, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN (added 2026-09-15, 227157d2c, after the gate of 2026-08-19, c9f1359e1). The Wayland code never reaches a Windows build, so the MinGW breakage the gate exists to prevent does not occur; the defect is that a registered gate is red in every test-enabled tree, so general-tests-ci.yml's unfiltered ctest would report it as a failure not on its one-name known-failure list (not executed in CI here). Either the Wayland sources should use System::Environment::SetEnvironmentVariable or the gate should scope out POSIX-only platform code.

items.text: The header of .github/workflows/d3d-windows-ci.yml still says CnaTests is not built on Windows because roughly ten test files call POSIX ::setenv(). At 009d40f5 those call sites were replaced with System::Environment::SetEnvironmentVariable (docs/cnatests-mingw-setenv-proposal.md) and a gate enforces the rule; the only remaining calls are in Wayland-only sources. The stated reason is documentation drift; whether an MSVC CnaTests build now works was not established.

input-ci.yml's comment says the CnaInputTests entry runs the input filter 'shuffled x3', but cmake/UnitTests.cmake registers it with --gtest_shuffle --gtest_repeat=5 (INPUT-BUILD-009). Comment drift only; the gate itself is correct.

Three comments quote registration counts that describe no configuration: cmake/TestHelpers.cmake ('~600 per-renderer CTest registrations'), cmake/UnitTests.cmake ('~330 existing test registrations') and general-tests-ci.yml ('~247 separately-registered renderer smoke-test' executables). No configure-independent registration count exists at 009d40f5. Comment drift only.

Besides the fopen macro, free-api's windows.h (reached through free-direct's <ddraw.h>) defines byte as BYTE (rpcndr.h, included unconditionally), maps about twenty Win32 names such as MessageBox, GetObject and LoadImage to their A variants, and defines RGB, TRUE/FALSE and MAX_PATH. In FreeDirectRenderer.cpp everything after the <ddraw.h> include sees them; a later-first-included header that spells std::byte or declares CNA::Devices::MessageBox would be rewritten. At 009d40f5 the file uses none of these names outside comments, and no CI job builds FREEDIRECT. Latent containment hazard, now documented on the free-direct deep dive; not a current defect.
